about: Kept by hand by incident.wikipedia@web-summit.dinis: the checkable statements of each Wikipedia page on Storm Charles, in our own English (a paraphrase, never Wikipedia's wording), each with an anchor (a few words of the article, to find the sentence in the revision named) and how it stands against this site. tools/wikipedia-claims.mjs reads this file, finds each sentence in the stored revision, attaches the footnotes it carries, and writes claims.json, compare.json and against.json. rel: 'matches' = a timeline row says the same; 'in-data' = this site holds it in a data file but no timeline row; 'missing' = nowhere on this site; 'behind' = Wikipedia states what a later official change has overtaken, and we hold the change; 'differs' = a figure or time differs. verdict: what this team found when it went to the primary source for the statement ('verified at primary source', 'press only', 'not established at source', or 'not checked by us'), with the row or decision that holds the check. Wikipedia is a lead for us, never the source.

topics.title: Who named the storm, and when

claims.anchor: às 13h17 UTC, o IPMA anunciou
claims.statement: IPMA announced the name Charles on 9 November at 13:17 UTC, for a low centred near 33° N, 31° W and moving east.

ours.note: The timeline now has the row (added 11 November after this comparison).
ours.verdict_note: IPMA communiqué no. 1, 13:17 UTC on 9 November (timeline row s-1109T1317, added after our first read reported it missing).

claims.anchor: com uma [[Pressão atmosférica|pressão]] central prevista de 991
claims.statement: Communiqué no. 1 forecast the centre near 34° N, 23° W, north of Madeira, at 00:00 UTC on 11 November, with a central pressure of 991 hPa.

ours.note: We hold the text of communiqué no. 2 only (data/weather/communiques.json); the first communiqué's position and pressure are not on this site.

claims.anchor: depressão de proveniência [[subtropical]]
claims.statement: Spain's AEMET described the system as a low of subtropical origin whose approach would worsen the weather over the Iberian Peninsula.

ours.note: Nothing on this site about the low's origin.

claims.anchor: localmente superior a 100 mm em 12 horas
claims.statement: For Madeira, IPMA forecast worsening from late 10 November to the morning of 11 November: persistent rain locally above 100 mm in 12 hours, south-west gusts of 80 to 100 km/h and up to 130 km/h on high ground, waves of 3.5 to 4.5 m on the south coast.

ours.note: Communiqué no. 1's Madeira figures are not on this site; no. 2's are (communiques.json).

claims.anchor: entre [[Sines]] e o [[Cabo Carvoeiro]]
claims.statement: For the mainland, IPMA's most likely track put the centre's passage between Sines and Cabo Carvoeiro, from late morning on 11 November, with gusts of 100 to 120 km/h (more in exposed places) and waves of four to six metres south of Cabo Carvoeiro.

ours.note: Our rows quote the same written track, and add what Wikipedia does not have: at 22:35 an IPMA meteorologist said on radio that the low should come in between Lisbon and Cabo de São Vicente, further south. The written communiqué had not changed when we last read it.
ours.verdict_note: The written track is in IPMA's communiqués as we hold them.

claims.anchor: às 17h07 UTC, o IPMA publicou o segundo comunicado
claims.statement: On 10 November at 17:07 UTC IPMA published communiqué no. 2, moving the forecast centre for 00:00 UTC on 11 November to about 34° N, 21° W at 989 hPa (it had been 34° N, 23° W at 991 hPa), still with high uncertainty.

ours.note: Same time and figures in our copy. The timeline now has the row s-1110T1707b.
ours.verdict_note: IPMA communiqué no. 2 (our copy: issued 17:07; the row says edited 17:07:58).

claims.anchor: altura máxima individual até 13 metros
claims.statement: Communiqué no. 2: Madeira gusts up to 140 km/h on high ground and south-coast waves of four to five metres; on the mainland gusts of 100 to 120 km/h, locally 140, rain that could pass 100 mm in 24 hours, and south of Cabo Raso waves of five to seven metres, the highest single wave up to 13 metres.

ours.note: In our copy of the communiqué's text.
ours.verdict_note: In the text of communiqué no. 2 as we hold it.

claims.anchor: entre as 21h00 desse dia e as 06h00 de 11 de Novembro
claims.statement: On 10 November IPMA raised to red the rain warning for Madeira's south coast and mountains, from 21:00 that day to 06:00 on 11 November, and issued a red wind warning for the mountains from 00:00 to 06:00.

ours.note: The decision graph has it, with IPMA's send time (07:24 UTC), which Wikipedia does not give.
ours.verdict_note: IPMA's CAP message (decision ipma-madeira-red, sent 07:24 UTC).

claims.anchor: programadas para as 08h00 e as 18h00
claims.statement: On 9 November Porto Santo Line cancelled the 08:00 and 18:00 sailings between Funchal and Porto Santo on 11 November and put on extra sailings on 10 November.

claims.anchor: todos os [[percursos pedestres]] classificados
claims.statement: On 10 November Madeira's forests institute closed all classified walking routes for the whole of 11 November, and the forest road between Eira do Serrado and Pico do Areeiro.

claims.anchor: com reabertura prevista para as 13h00
claims.statement: The regional government closed Madeira's schools for the morning of 11 November, reopening at 13:00.

claims.anchor: três navios de cruzeiro
claims.statement: The ports authority said three cruise ships cancelled their calls at Funchal on 11 November; six calls had been cancelled over the previous days, counting Bruna.

claims.anchor: cancelou dez voos de e para a Madeira
claims.statement: On 10 November TAP cancelled ten flights to and from Madeira: every Lisbon and Porto link between 00:00 and 12:00 on 11 November.

ours.note: We have ANA's notice that operations would be affected, not TAP's count.
ours.verdict_note: The count of ten is not established: the press we read says only that several TAP flights to Funchal were affected, from the airport operator's site; TAP's own statement is about rebooking (decision tap-adjusts).

claims.anchor: entre as 16h30 de 10 de Novembro e as 12h00 do dia seguinte
claims.statement: Madeira's fisheries directorate closed all fish markets and cold stores from 16:30 on 10 November to 12:00 the next day; Funchal suspended waste collection and closed its cultural venues from 16:00 to 13:00; the health service suspended non-urgent appointments until 12:00; the bus company suspended seven routes until 13:00.

claims.anchor: adiamento dos 34 julgamentos
claims.statement: Madeira's courts were closed for the whole of 11 November by order of the presiding judge, postponing 34 trials.

ours.note: The article names the judge; we do not repeat the name.
ours.verdict_note: As stated, not established: the order we could trace is national (court presidents may close courts fully or partly; decision csm-courts), not specific to Madeira. The 34 trials were not checked.

claims.anchor: alargou à costa norte da Madeira o aviso vermelho
claims.statement: On 10 November IPMA extended the red rain warning to Madeira's north coast, putting the whole island at the highest level until 06:00 on 11 November; Porto Santo stayed orange.

claims.anchor: colocou oito distritos sob aviso vermelho de vento
claims.statement: On the morning of 10 November IPMA put eight districts under a red wind warning for the next day: Beja, Faro and Setúbal from 09:00 to 21:00; Évora, Leiria, Lisboa, Portalegre and Santarém from 12:00 to 21:00; gusts could reach 140 km/h in the most exposed places.

ours.note: Lisbon's hours agreed when written. Since then IPMA lowered the wind warnings (sent 07:16:30 UTC on 11 November): Lisboa, Setúbal and Beja red to orange, 09:00 to 21:00; Leiria, Santarém, Portalegre and Évora red to yellow. The Portuguese article (revision of 10:17 UTC) still gives eight districts at red and says nothing of the change. Wikipedia says 'in the morning'; we have the minute IPMA sent the red warning, 07:18 UTC on 10 November, from its CAP message.
ours.verdict_note: Lisbon's red wind from IPMA's CAP message, sent 07:18 UTC (row s-1110T0718). The other seven districts were not checked by us.

claims.anchor: Na actualização dos avisos meteorológicos das 16h30 UTC
claims.statement: In its 16:30 UTC update on 10 November IPMA issued red rain warnings for Castelo Branco, Leiria, Lisboa, Portalegre, Santarém and Setúbal, valid 12:00 to 18:00 on 11 November: nine mainland districts at red in all, eight for wind and six for rain.

ours.note: (1) Our row s-1110T1742 now says IPMA sent it at 16:30:01 and that 17:42 is when the desk read it (corrected after this comparison). (2) At 21:23 IPMA moved Lisbon's red rain to 09:00 to 18:00. Wikipedia's revision of 01:33 on 11 November still says 12:00, although this footnote was consulted on 11 November.
ours.verdict_note: Sent 16:30:01 by IPMA's CAP message for Lisbon; and overtaken at 21:23 (row s-1110T2353). The other five districts were not checked by us.

claims.anchor: declaração da situação de alerta pelo [[Governo português]]
claims.statement: The lead: the storm's approach led to red warnings for Madeira and nine mainland districts and to the government declaring an alert situation for 11 November, with schools and non-essential public services closed as a precaution.

ours.verdict_note: The government's own page, timed 12:10 (row s-1110T1210).

claims.anchor: anunciou o encerramento preventivo de estabelecimentos de ensino
claims.statement: On 10 November the government declared the alert situation for 11 November; the Interior Minister announced the closing of schools and non-essential public services, the suspension of outdoor activities and limits on parks, forests and gardens, and asked people to stay at home.

ours.note: Wikipedia gives the day only. We have that it was announced at about 09:17 and that the government's page is timed 12:10, and the hours (00:00 to 23:59).
ours.verdict_note: The government's own page (row s-1110T1210); the announcement at about 09:17 is from live blogs (evidence).

claims.anchor: entre as 10h00 e as 23h59
claims.statement: Rede Expressos suspended all its coach services on 11 November from 10:00 to 23:59, with automatic refunds.

ours.note: In the decision graph; no timeline row.

claims.anchor: publicou um aviso à população relativo à Charles
claims.statement: ANEPC published a warning to the population (Aviso 21) on the risks of rain and strong wind, with self-protection measures.

ours.note: The timeline now has the row.
ours.verdict_note: ANEPC's Aviso 21 (row s-1109T2030, added after our first read).

claims.anchor: identificou 101 municípios do continente
claims.statement: The environment agency (APA) identified 101 mainland municipalities at higher risk of floods and urban flooding; its president pointed to urban areas of the Algarve, the Oeste and the Centro.

ours.note: Not on this site in any file.
ours.verdict_note: No such notice was found on the environment agency's own site by incident.researcher@ (01:45 to 01:50 UTC on 11 November). The figure rests on the radio report Wikipedia cites.

claims.anchor: a partir das 00h00 do dia 11
claims.statement: Lisbon's city council announced the closing of the city's road tunnels from 00:00 on 11 November.

claims.anchor: redução da velocidade máxima para 60 km/h
claims.statement: Lusoponte cut the speed limit to 60 km/h on the 25 de Abril and Vasco da Gama bridges and advised against motorcycles and vehicles exposed to wind.

claims.anchor: encerramento preventivo dos espaços museológicos
claims.statement: The public company Museus e Monumentos de Portugal closed its museums and monuments on 11 November, with rebooking or refunds.

ours.note: Now in the decision graph as evidence.
ours.verdict_note: Dated press quoting the company's online message (decision mmp-closed, evidence).

claims.anchor: cerca de 1 100 militares
claims.statement: The GNR set up an operational reserve of about 1,100 officers on standby.

ours.note: Now in the decision graph as evidence.
ours.verdict_note: GNR's own site lists a notice of that date; the figure 1,100 is the press quoting it (decision gnr-readiness, evidence).

claims.anchor: quatro estações e do interface das Olaias
claims.statement: Lisbon's Metro opened four stations and the Olaias interchange as night shelter for homeless people on the nights of 10 to 11 and 11 to 12 November.

claims.anchor: cancelamento integral das actividades previstas para 11 de Novembro
claims.statement: Web Summit's organisers announced on 10 November that all of 11 November, the conference's second day, was cancelled, after recommendations from the government and the civil protection authorities, and said they meant to resume on 12 November if the weather allowed.

ours.note: Wikipedia cites ECO and gives no time. We have the organisers' own page (published 19:09 UTC) and ECO's article 32 minutes later (19:41). 'If the weather allows' is the press's wording; the organisers wrote that they aim to proceed as planned.
ours.verdict_note: The organisers' own page, published 19:09 UTC (row s-1110T1909).

claims.anchor: sobrepondo-se aos efeitos ainda presentes da depressão Bruna
claims.statement: AEMET forecast worse weather over the Iberian Peninsula as Charles approached on 11 November, on top of Bruna: heavy rain, strong wind and rough seas, mostly in the south and west of Spain.

claims.anchor: estavam associados principalmente às frentes da Bruna
claims.statement: The red rain warnings of 10 November in Cáceres and Ávila were tied mainly to Bruna's fronts, before Charles arrived.

claims.anchor: registou 47,6 mm de precipitação numa hora
claims.statement: By 21:00 on 10 November IPMA's station at Chão do Areeiro had measured 47.6 mm in one hour and 91.7 mm in six, above the red thresholds for both; 13 of IPMA's 18 stations on the island were at some warning level.

claims.anchor: foram registadas 313 ocorrências
claims.statement: Madeira's regional civil protection counted 313 incidents linked to the storm between 20:00 on 10 November and 16:00 on 11 November: 84 landslides, 76 floodings, 48 fallen trees, 11 collapsed structures; 779 mobilisations of responders and 328 of vehicles; Funchal 75, Santa Cruz 67. (Earlier counts in the article: 291 to 14:00 until 16:34 UTC; 235 to 11:00 until 15:01; 205 to 09:00 until 14:48; 71 to 02:00 until 09:48; 38 to 23:30 until 03:25.)

ours.verdict_note: Our rows hold 71 to 02:00, 99 and 162 at 06:50, each as evidence from the press. Wikipedia's 313 to 16:00 is from the regional daily reporting civil protection's count: a lead for the researcher, not a fact.
ours.note: Wikipedia is ahead of our rows: a later count.

claims.anchor: 122 mm de precipitação em três horas e 133,9 mm em seis horas
claims.statement: By 22:00 Chão do Areeiro had 122 mm in three hours, 133.9 mm in six and 50.7 mm in one; four other stations were also at red thresholds.

ours.note: Wikipedia was the lead; the figure was then checked at IPMA's station data and the row added.
ours.verdict_note: IPMA's own station data: exactly 133.9 mm in the six hours to 22:00 at Areeiro, and 230.5 mm in the six hours to 01:00 (row s-1111T0146). The reading of the hour labels is our inference, stated in madeira.json.

claims.anchor: encerramento da Rua Cardeal Tolentino Mendonça
claims.statement: In Machico a street by the marina was closed after a flood and a landslide partly blocked it.

claims.anchor: falhas no fornecimento de electricidade e dificuldades nas comunicações
claims.statement: On Porto Santo there were power failures and trouble with communications as the low passed; the mayor confirmed the municipal civil protection centre was activated, coastal accesses closed and operations at the harbour suspended.

ours.verdict_note: Our row reports a front-page headline on the power cuts (title only). The measures the mayor confirmed are not on this site.
ours.note: The article names the mayor; our claim gives the role.

claims.anchor: O sistema passou mais a sul da ilha
claims.statement: On the morning of 11 November the assistant commander of Madeira's regional civil protection said that, on the weather information available, the storm's most intense period had passed Madeira; the system passed further south of the island and weaker than first forecast; the streams' flows, up overnight, were back to normal, with the rescue services still mobilised.

ours.note: Not on this site as a statement by Madeira's civil protection. Our row s-1111T0822 holds an analysis (a hypothesis) that the centre passed close to Madeira airport between about 07:30 and 08:00: a different statement, not checked against this one. The article names the officer; our claim gives the role. This is about Madeira; it is not IPMA's statement of 22:35 on the mainland track (s-1110T2235), which the article's text still lacks.

claims.anchor: havia acumulado 355 mm de precipitação em 12 horas
claims.statement: By the records published up to 04:00 on 11 November, Chão do Areeiro had 355 mm of rain in 12 hours, 237.1 mm in six hours and 56.5 mm in one hour; six other stations passed the red threshold for six hours (São Vicente 143.2 mm, Santo da Serra 132.4, Pico do Areeiro 125, Pico Alto 119.7, Monte 88.4, Prazeres 78.5); gusts since midnight of 136 km/h at Chão do Areeiro, 126 at the airport, 122 at Caniçal and 108 at Pico Alto.

ours.verdict_note: Our row is our own reading of IPMA's station Areeiro: 249.5 mm in six hours at 07:27 (232.1 mm at our 04:23 read), close to Wikipedia's 237.1 mm to 04:00 but not the same figure or hour. The 12-hour total, the other stations and the gusts are not on this site; the regional daily's figures were not checked by us against IPMA's data.
ours.note: Same station and measure; different hours.

claims.anchor: acumulou 502,7 mm de precipitação em 24 horas
claims.statement: From IPMA's records to 09:00 on 11 November, Chão do Areeiro had 502.7 mm of rain in 24 hours (406.9 mm in 12 hours; maxima of 249.5 mm in six hours and 65.4 mm in one hour); eight stations passed the red threshold for six hours; next in 24 hours: Pico do Areeiro 265.9, Pico Alto 262, Santo da Serra 256.7, São Vicente 252.1 mm. (Until the (revision of 14:48 UTC on 11 November) this claim was the regional president's 479 mm in 12 hours, which the article no longer carries.)

ours.note: The six-hour maximum, 249.5 mm, is our row s-1111T0727 (IPMA's station Areeiro, read by us); the 24- and 12-hour totals are not on this site. Cited to the regional daily, not to IPMA's own data.

claims.anchor: foi resgatado com vida perto das 08h00
claims.statement: On the morning of 11 November a man of 78 was swept away when a stream overflowed in São Roque, Funchal; first given as missing, he was rescued alive near 08:00 by volunteer firefighters with the police, with signs of hypothermia and no serious injury (two footnotes: the regional public broadcaster and the regional daily).

ours.note: Not on this site. A private person, not named by Wikipedia or by us.

claims.anchor: estavam confirmados 16 voos cancelados numa consulta efectuada às 06h50
claims.statement: Funchal's bus operator suspended its service on the morning of 11 November because of the rain and the risk of streams overflowing; at Madeira airport 16 flights were confirmed cancelled at a check made at 06:50, and access to Funchal's centre was restricted for safety.

ours.verdict_note: Our row reports the same 16 cancelled flights (the airport operator's site, read 06:50) and the closing of access to Funchal's centre (civil protection's communiqué, through a news agency), as evidence. The bus suspension is not on this site.
ours.note: The same figures at the same hour, from the press.

claims.anchor: três famílias foram obrigadas a abandonar as respectivas habitações
claims.statement: In Serra de Água (Ribeira Brava) three families had to leave their homes after a stream overflowed and flooded four houses when a culvert was blocked; the mayor confirmed they went to relatives and that nobody was hurt. The same revisions add: five incidents on Porto Santo confirmed by its council; the parish council's offices in Machico flooded to about one metre; power cuts in Santa Cruz, Machico and Santana after a high-voltage cable fell; roads closed in Machico and Porto Moniz.

ours.note: None of these is on this site. Each has one footnote, the regional daily.

claims.anchor: activou o nível de alerta máximo por vento na ilha de [[La Palma]]
claims.statement: On 10 November the Government of the Canary Islands activated its highest alert level for wind on La Palma and the high ground of Tenerife, from 00:00 on 11 November, with alerts for rough seas and rain and preventive measures against floods and landslides; AEMET issued a red wind warning for La Palma for the morning of 11 November (two footnotes: the Canary Islands government's own notice, and a Spanish online daily).

ours.note: Not on this site. The first footnote is the deciding body's own notice, which is rare in this article; neither it nor AEMET's warning was read by us.
ours.verdict_note: The Canary Islands' alert was not read at source (noted in decision aemet-special).

claims.anchor: rajadas de vento até 162 km/h em [[Santa Cruz de La Palma]]
claims.statement: A new section, Spain (added at 10:17 UTC on 11 November): on the morning of 11 November the Canary Islands' public television reported gusts up to 162 km/h at Santa Cruz de La Palma and over 130 km/h at Izaña, Tenerife; three roads closed on La Palma; a fault on a power line at 07:12 cut supply to 17,622 customers in three municipalities, restored at 07:34; a ferry operator cancelled several crossings; fallen trees closed roads on Gran Canaria.

ours.note: Not on this site: the Canary Islands are outside what this timeline follows. One footnote, the islands' public broadcaster; the hours are presumably local time (the article does not say).

claims.anchor: nomeada quatro dias antes, sendo dois sistemas independentes
claims.statement: Charles came during unsettled weather also tied to Bruna, named four days earlier; they are two independent systems.

ours.note: IPMA's communiqué no. 2 says Bruna is a system independent of Charles.
ours.verdict_note: IPMA's communiqué no. 2 says so.

claims.anchor: a few hundred miles south of [[Bermuda]]
claims.statement: The storm began as a non-tropical low over the western subtropical Atlantic, formed on a weakening front a few hundred miles south of Bermuda in early November.

ours.verdict_note: The Hurricane Center's archived outlooks were read by incident.meteorologist@ (analysis.md, section 8b): a low expected from 2 November, the chance rising to 50% by 4 November. These exact figures were not compared one by one.

claims.anchor: initially giving it a 10% chance of development within 48 hours
claims.statement: The US National Hurricane Center began following it in its outlooks on 3 November, at a 10% chance of development within 48 hours and 30% within seven days.

ours.verdict_note: The Hurricane Center's archived outlooks were read by incident.meteorologist@ (analysis.md, section 8b): a low expected from 2 November, the chance rising to 50% by 4 November. These exact figures were not compared one by one.

claims.anchor: had lowered both chances to 20%
claims.statement: By 6 November the Center had lowered both chances to 20%, saying the low might only briefly become subtropical before another low absorbed it.

ours.verdict_note: The Hurricane Center's archived outlooks were read by incident.meteorologist@ (analysis.md, section 8b): a low expected from 2 November, the chance rising to 50% by 4 November. These exact figures were not compared one by one.

claims.anchor: labelled the low as Invest 94L
claims.statement: On 7 November the Center's outlook labelled the low Invest 94L, several hundred miles south-south-east of Bermuda.

ours.note: A hidden note left in the wikitext by an editor says the sources do not state that 94L became Charles and asks for it to be checked. Wikipedia itself marks this as unverified.
ours.verdict_note: The Hurricane Center's own archived outlooks label the low AL94 on 6 November (11:37 UTC), not 7; and no source read says it became Charles (data/weather/analysis.md, section 8b, a hypothesis).

claims.anchor: Charles retained its subtropical origins as it crossed the Atlantic
claims.statement: Charles kept its subtropical origins as it crossed the Atlantic under the subtropical jet, leaving heavy rain from near Bermuda onward. Footnoted to a Spanish weather site (Meteored); until the revision of 18:12 UTC on 11 November the sentence named it in the text ("According to the Spanish weather service Meteored"), an edit whose summary says it removes reference to any particular medium.

claims.anchor: was officially named on 9 November 2026
claims.statement: IPMA named Storm Charles on 9 November 2026.

ours.note: English gives the day; Portuguese and our row give 13:17 UTC.
ours.verdict_note: As w-pt-01.

claims.anchor: described Charles as a small but deep low-pressure system
claims.statement: AEMET described Charles as a small but deep low expected to cross Spain quickly with very heavy rain and strong winds, its track uncertain.

claims.anchor: Red warnings, the highest level, were issued in Portugal
claims.statement: Red warnings were issued in Portugal (mainland and Madeira) and in Spain.

ours.note: For Portugal. The sentence carries no footnote in the article.

claims.anchor: IPMA issued orange warnings for rain, wind and rough seas
claims.statement: IPMA issued orange warnings for rain, wind and rough seas in several mainland districts including Lisbon, with gusts up to 120 km/h and waves up to 6 m.

ours.note: The earlier state. Our rows record the orange rain around the red window; the reds followed.

claims.anchor: red warnings were in place for wind in eight mainland districts and for rain in six
claims.statement: By the afternoon of 10 November red warnings were in place for wind in eight mainland districts and for rain in six; the coast from Leiria through Lisbon to Setúbal was among the most exposed.

ours.note: The footnote is a newsletter on Substack.

claims.anchor: while the red rain warnings ran from 12:00 to 18:00
claims.statement: The red wind warnings for 11 November ran 09:00 to 21:00 in Beja, Faro and Setúbal and 12:00 to 21:00 in Évora, Leiria, Lisbon, Portalegre and Santarém; the red rain warnings ran 12:00 to 18:00 in Castelo Branco, Leiria, Lisbon, Portalegre, Santarém and Setúbal.

ours.note: Lisbon's red rain was moved to 09:00 to 18:00 at 21:23 on 10 November; the English page was last edited at 20:32 and still says 12:00. Lisbon's red wind was lowered to orange, 09:00 to 21:00, at 07:16:30 on 11 November; the English page (last edited 02:22) still gives red, 12:00 to 21:00.
ours.verdict_note: Lisbon's windows from IPMA's CAP messages; the rain window was overtaken at 21:23 on 10 November and the wind level at 07:16:30 on 11 November.

claims.anchor: make landfall between Cabo Carvoeiro and [[Sines]]
claims.statement: IPMA expected the storm to make landfall between Cabo Carvoeiro and Sines.

ours.note: As w-pt-05: the written track; we also hold the 22:35 spoken line that puts it further south.

claims.anchor: while the north coast was under an orange warning
claims.statement: In Madeira a red warning was in force for the mountains and the south coast from 21:00 on 10 November to 06:00 on 11 November, with gusts up to 130 km/h on high ground; the north coast was under orange. A separate red wind warning covered the mountains from 00:00 to 06:00, gusts up to 140 km/h.

ours.verdict_note: The south coast and mountains from IPMA's CAP message (ipma-madeira-red). The north coast's level was not checked by us.

claims.anchor: declared a state of alert for all of mainland Portugal from 00:00 to 23:59
claims.statement: The Portuguese government declared a state of alert for all of mainland Portugal from 00:00 to 23:59 on 11 November; ANEPC raised its readiness to the highest level; schools and non-essential public services on the mainland closed for the day.

ours.note: Same hours as our row. No time of announcement in Wikipedia.
ours.verdict_note: The government's own page for the hours and the closures (row s-1110T1210). ANEPC's readiness level is in the decision graph (anepc-readiness).

claims.anchor: from 09:00 to 23:59 local time, in the north of the province
claims.statement: In Spain a red rain warning ran on 10 November from 09:00 to 23:59 local time in the north of Cáceres and the south of Ávila, with up to 120 mm in 12 hours forecast.

claims.anchor: in 32 municipalities in the south of Ávila
claims.statement: Castile and León suspended school and imposed its strictest limits on movement in 32 municipalities in the south of Ávila, home to about 49,000 people.

claims.anchor: issued special warning 38/2026
claims.statement: On the evening of 9 November AEMET issued special warning 38/2026 for 10 to 12 November, for the south and west of the peninsula and the Canary Islands, citing Bruna and Charles together.

ours.note: Now in the decision graph.
ours.verdict_note: In part: a special warning is in force on AEMET's own warnings page (title read 01:46 UTC on 11 November; decision aemet-special). Its number and its period were not readable there and rest on the press Wikipedia cites.

claims.anchor: probably through Portugal, on 11 November
claims.statement: Charles was expected to enter the peninsula, probably through Portugal, on 11 November, and to weaken from 12 November as it moved north-east.

ours.note: We publish no statement about what follows landfall beyond IPMA's and the airport forecast's hours.

claims.anchor: declared a wind alert across the whole archipelago from 18:00
claims.statement: The Government of the Canary Islands declared a wind alert for the whole archipelago from 18:00 local time on 10 November.

ours.verdict_note: The Canary Islands' alert was not read at source (noted in decision aemet-special).

claims.anchor: could locally exceed
claims.statement: AEMET forecast orange wind warnings on all eight islands on 11 November, with gusts that could pass 130 km/h on La Palma and Tenerife.

claims.anchor: | area affected = [[Portugal]] (including [[Madeira]]), [[Spain]]
claims.statement: The infobox lists the areas affected as Portugal (with Madeira), Spain (with the Canary Islands), France and Italy, and the duration as 9 November to the present.

ours.note: France and Italy have no footnote and no sentence in the section. This site covers Lisbon.

claims.anchor: '''Impacts'''
claims.statement: The 'Impacts' heading of the English section is empty.

ours.note: Nothing to match: no claim is made.

claims.anchor: minpressure   = {{convert|994|hPa
claims.statement: The Chinese infobox gives a lowest pressure of 994 hPa (995 hPa until the revision of 08:28 UTC on 11 November; the season table gained the same 994 hPa at 08:45).

ours.note: No footnote, before or after the change from 995. Our analysis quotes a model's forecast minimum (986.7 hPa, met.no, a hypothesis row: s-1111T0000); nobody has published a measured minimum that we have read.

claims.anchor: 指出查爾斯和布魯娜風暴是獨立的氣象系統
claims.statement: On 9 November IPMA said Charles and Bruna are independent weather systems.

claims.anchor: | area affected = [[葡萄牙]]
claims.statement: The Chinese infobox lists Portugal, Spain (with the Canary Islands), France and Italy as affected.

ours.note: As the English infobox; no footnote.

claims.anchor: |lowest pressure=999
claims.statement: The Vietnamese section (an infobox only, no prose, added 12:23 UTC on 11 November) gives a lowest pressure of 999 hPa.

ours.note: No footnote; differs from the Chinese 994 hPa. Nobody has published a measured minimum that we have read.

claims.anchor: |Formed=02 tháng 11
claims.statement: The Vietnamese infobox says the storm formed on 2 November and dissipated on 3 November.

ours.note: No footnote. Our timeline has the storm named and reaching Madeira and the mainland from 10 November; these dates look like a template left unfilled (our reading, a hypothesis).

claims.anchor: publicou o terceiro comunicado especial relativo à Charles
claims.statement: On 11 November IPMA published its third special communiqué: the low had split into two distinct cores, unlike the numerical models' first forecast, which should reduce its deepening and the wind on the mainland; persistent, at times heavy rain still expected, gusts of 70 to 90 km/h in the south, up to 110 km/h on exposed coasts and high ground. Cited to IPMA's communiqués page.

ours.note: Entered Wikipedia at 14:48 UTC, about two and a half hours after IPMA published it (12:16) and our row (12:26).

claims.anchor: registavam 222 voos cancelados
claims.statement: In a new section 'Portugal continental' (the article's first on the mainland's effects): 222 flights cancelled at Lisbon (208) and Faro (14) by ANA's data read at 09:20 on 11 November. Cited to RTP.

ours.note: The same 09:20 figure is our row s-1111T1037 (via CNN Portugal); our row s-1111T1236 has a later count from the press at 12:32 to 12:35. Neither read at ANA itself.

claims.anchor: abandonou preventivamente o porto do Funchal
claims.statement: On the morning of 11 November the Porto Santo ferry left Funchal harbour as a precaution at about 06:30 after some mooring lines broke in the wind, and sheltered off Madeira's north coast (the operator's administrator, by role).

ours.note: Not on this site. Cited to the regional daily.

claims.anchor: cerca de 400 clientes estiveram temporariamente sem serviço em Machico
claims.statement: A telecoms operator said about 400 customers in Machico were briefly without service after power cuts; restored; isolated faults remained in Porto Moniz and Ponta do Sol on the morning of 11 November.

ours.note: Not on this site. Cited to the regional daily.

claims.anchor: confirmou a interrupção da circulação ferroviária na [[Linha da Beira Baixa]]
claims.statement: On the afternoon of 11 November the national railway confirmed the Beira Baixa line interrupted between Santa Margarida and Tramagal by a landslip, Lisbon urban trains suppressed between Campolide and Alcântara-Terra, and four Intercity trains over the 25 de Abril bridge suppressed as a precaution. Cited to RTP.

ours.note: Our rows read CP's own notice (13:30 and 16:31 updates).

claims.anchor: At least one person has died in the [[Canary Islands]]
claims.statement: From 16:40 UTC on 11 November the English section says at least one person has died in the Canary Islands, and its infobox gives 3 fatalities in the same revision. The sentence cites a bare link to an English-language Canarian news site; the infobox figure has no footnote.

ours.note: No death is on this site: no row of ours reports one, in Portugal, Madeira or the Canaries. A lead to check at the authorities (Spain's 112 Canarias, the Canary government), not a fact; the page disagrees with itself (1 in the text, 3 in the infobox).

differences.what: Madeira's north coast: Portuguese says the red rain warning was extended to the north coast, so the whole island was at red; English still says the north coast was under orange.
differences.reading: English is the older state: its page was last edited at 20:32 on 10 November. A hypothesis from the edit times, not a finding about IPMA.
differences.label: hypothesis

differences.what: Who called the low subtropical in origin: Portuguese attributes it to AEMET, Spain's state agency (citing Cadena SER); English attributes it to Meteored, which it calls 'the Spanish weather service' (citing Meteored's own site).
differences.reading: Two different bodies. AEMET is Spain's state meteorological agency; Meteored is a separate, commercial forecaster. English's label for Meteored is loose.
differences.label: hypothesis

differences.what: Central pressure: Portuguese gives IPMA's forecast for 00:00 UTC on 11 November, 991 hPa in communiqué no. 1 and 989 hPa in no. 2. Chinese gives a lowest pressure of 994 hPa (995 until 08:28 UTC on 11 November) with no footnote. English leaves the field empty. Vietnamese (from 12:23 UTC on 11 November) gives 999 hPa, also with no footnote.
differences.reading: Not the same quantity: a forecast for one hour against a 'minimum'. The Chinese figure cannot be checked from the page.
differences.label: hypothesis

differences.what: Areas affected: the English and Chinese infoboxes list Portugal, Spain, France and Italy; the Portuguese infobox lists Madeira and mainland Portugal only.
differences.reading: France and Italy carry no footnote in either page.
differences.label: hypothesis

differences.what: The naming: Portuguese gives the minute (9 November, 13:17 UTC) and the position; English gives the day.
differences.reading: They agree; Portuguese is more exact. Both cite IPMA's communiqués index page, an address whose content changes.
differences.label: evidence

differences.what: The alert situation: English gives its hours (00:00 to 23:59 on 11 November) and ANEPC's readiness at the highest level; Portuguese gives neither, but names the minister and lists the measures.
differences.label: evidence

differences.what: Lisbon's red rain warning: both say 12:00 to 18:00.
differences.reading: Both are behind IPMA, which moved it to 09:00 to 18:00 at 21:23 UTC on 10 November (our row s-1110T2353, from IPMA's CAP message).
differences.label: fact

differences.what: Deaths: English (from 16:40 UTC on 11 November) says 'at least one' in the Canary Islands in its text and 3 in its infobox; Portuguese, Chinese and Vietnamese report none (the Vietnamese infobox: 'no information yet').
differences.reading: The English infobox and text disagree within one revision; neither figure is from an authority. A hypothesis about the page, not a finding about the storm.
differences.label: hypothesis

our_facts.fact: Web Summit's Day 2 (Wednesday 11 November) will not take place: the organisers' own page, published 19:09 UTC on 10 November.
our_facts.label: fact

our_facts.label: evidence for 09:17; fact for 12:10

our_facts.fact: At 21:23 UTC on 10 November IPMA moved Lisbon's red rain warning three hours earlier: Wednesday 09:00 to 18:00.
our_facts.label: fact

our_facts.fact: At 07:16:30 UTC on 11 November IPMA lowered Lisbon's wind warning from red to orange and started it three hours earlier: 09:00 to 21:00, gusts up to 120 km/h.
our_facts.label: fact

our_facts.fact: At 22:35 UTC on 10 November an IPMA meteorologist said on Rádio Observador that the low should come in between the Lisbon region and Cabo de São Vicente, further south than the written communiqué.
our_facts.label: evidence (words said on air)

patterns.pt: Cabo de São Vicente|Sagres|mais a sul do (país|continente|território)

our_facts.pattern_note: Narrowed at the 09:54 UTC read of 11 November: 'mais a sul' alone matched the new sentence about the system passing south of Madeira (claim w-pt-38), which is not this fact. The Portuguese article still says nothing in its text about a landfall further south on the mainland; one new footnote (a public broadcaster's article, for the cancelled flights) has 'possível mudança de trajetória para sul' in its title only.
